newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-ZOELLER WITHDRAWS FROM GREATER GREENSBORO CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ZOELLER WITHDRAWS FROM GREATER GREENSBORO CLASSIC.

text.p: Fuzzy Zoeller, who made controversial remarks about Tiger Woods on the final day of the Masters, officially withdrew Wednesday from this week's Greater Greensboro Classic.
Zoeller spoke briefly to reporters and said he will not play in a tournament until he has an opportunity to speak with Woods.

"I started this, and I feel strongly that I have to make things right with Tiger first before anything else," said Zoeller in a statement. "I also regret the distraction this has caused the world of golf."
Zoeller also said Wednesday he was advised not to answer questions from reporters about the controversy.
Zoeller's controversial remarks were made on the final day of the Masters, but the interview was broadcast a week later on CNN's Sunday show, "Pro Golf Weekly."

"That little boy is driving well and he's putting well," Zoeller told CNN. "He's doing everything it takes to win. So, you know what you guys do when he gets in here? You pat him on the back and say, 'Congratulations' and, 'Enjoy it' and tell him not to serve fried chicken next year."
Zoeller then snapped his fingers, turned to walk away, and added, "Or collard greens or whatever the hell they serve."
The 21-year-old Woods, who became the youngest winner of the Masters and the first minority golfer to win a major championship, is not entered in the Greensboro tournament.
Zoeller apologised Monday for the remarks.
"My comments were not intended to be racially derogatory, and I apologise for the fact that they were misconstrued in that fashion," Zoeller said in a statement.
PGA Tour Commissioner Tim Finchem also issued a statement on Wednesday.
"The statement made today by Fuzzy Zoeller, in my judgment, more accurately reflects his true feelings as expressed to me personally," Finchem said.

"He recognises that the comments made at Augusta were inappropriate, unacceptable and deeply offensive to a great many people. By making this additional statement, I think he has demonstrated how deep his concerns are regarding the inappropriateness of these comments.
"I believe his decision to withdraw from the Greater Greensboro Chrysler Classic is the right decision."
On Tuesday, the Kmart discount department store chain dropped its sponsorship of PGA Tour veteran Zoeller, saying it was concerned over racial jokes he made about Woods.
